name: Binance USD-M BTCUSDT perpetual mark one-minute Wilder ATR(14)
description: A causal reading over the fresh Binance USD-M BTCUSDT perpetual mark price, taken from either the socket `markPrice` stream or the REST `premiumIndex` poll that carries the same mark state (F2/E50), sampled once per second on the lane decision clock. Each one-second sample holds the venue's latest mark row for up to a 3-second bound (a research default; the premium-index poll lands about every 1.3 seconds and Bybit mark prices carry multi-second gaps), and a mark row 3 seconds or more old is a missing sample, so a stalled poll or an absent mark invalidates the bar spanning it and re-warms the identity. Atr is Wilder's average true range over fourteen one-minute bars. True range is the greatest of the bar's high minus its low, the absolute difference between its high and the previous bar's close, and the absolute difference between its low and the previous bar's close. The first average is the arithmetic mean of the first fourteen true ranges and every later one is Wilder's smoothing, previous average plus (current true range minus previous average) divided by fourteen. atr_bps is atr divided by the latest bar close, times ten thousand, and is scale-free. close is that latest bar close and bar_count the number of contiguous closed bars behind the reading. The fourteen-bar period is the standard Wilder length and is an initial research default that requires empirical calibration; the true-range and smoothing formulas are not heuristic thresholds. One-minute bars are closed on the lane decision clock at minute boundaries from the one-second sample series: open is the first sample of the minute, high and low its extrema, close its last sample. A bar that is missing any one-second sample is invalid; the missing sample breaks continuity, every retained bar and every smoothed state derived from them is discarded, and the bar warm-up restarts from the next whole bar. Nothing is bridged across a gap. Ready once fifteen contiguous one-minute bars have closed (fourteen true ranges need fifteen closes). Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even. Every reading is causal: it reads only samples at or before the decision it is published on. E47 (USD quoting): this identity quotes in USD. Its price-level fields (`atr`, `close`) are converted from the venue's USDT quote through the Kraken USDT/USD reference midpoint at decision time, and the rate and its age are published as usdt_usd_rate and usdt_usd_rate_age_ms; an absent or stale reference forces the identity non-ready with `usdt_reference_stale`. Its remaining outputs are basis-point ratios, counts and timestamps and are quote-currency neutral. quote_currency is the constant "usd". Binance inputs are rights-gated (`signals/knowledge/RIGHTS-LEDGER.md`): the lane is built and tested to the adopted standard, and its runtime refuses to start unless the environment allow-list `SIGNALS_ENABLED_VENUES` names `binance`. The Binance USD-M socket `markPrice` stream is unreachable from the Tokyo box (E30), so the mark state is fed by the REST `premiumIndex` poll (F2/E50); before the first mark row of a generation this identity publishes the honest unavailable reason `binance_recovery_required` rather than a warm-up that could never resolve. Adopted in the C3a TA pack (ruling E51, 2026-09-04): the seven technical-analysis identities are published on every price venue we carry, computed from the venue's own one-second sample ring by the shared `crates/btc-signals/src/ta.rs` helper, so every scope runs byte-identical arithmetic and only the sample series differs.
